title: Metabolomics as the missing piece in epigenetics research
content: The study of epigenetics has revolutionized our understanding of how environment, diet, and lifestyle influence health [1, 2]. Experience-dependent and potentially heritable epigenetic mechanisms, such as DNA methylation [3], histone modifications [4], and the activity of non-coding RNA [5], regulate the expression of genes involved in cell function, development, aging, and disease [6, 7]. These mechanisms, explored through genomic and transcriptomic approaches, have traditionally been the primary focus of epigenetic research [8]. However, metabolomics, the study of small molecules (metabolites) involved in cellular processes, represents a promising yet underexplored component of the epigenetic landscape [9].
